monthly.summary: Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 40.8mm of rain in August 2026, roughly 0.9 times the August long-term average of around 48mm and in line with near-average conditions for the month. Rain fell on 12 days, with 6 of those exceeding 1mm. The wettest stretch came at the end of the month, when 19.0mm fell between 29 and 31 August, including 15.4mm on 30 August, the only day above 10mm; 22 August brought 8.1mm and 5 August brought 5.0mm. Looking ahead, a positive Indian Ocean Dipole alongside a strengthening El Niño is a combination that normally enhances rainfall in the Greater Horn of Africa, and ICPAC expects wetter-than-normal conditions in the October to December 2026 season.

Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 122.2mm of rain in September 2026, roughly 3.5 times the long-term September average of around 35mm and well above normal for the month. Rain fell on 21 days, with five days exceeding 10mm, and the heaviest were 27.7mm on 11 September, 24.1mm on 18 September and 20.2mm on 27 September. Rainfall was concentrated in the middle of the month, with 58.7mm falling between 17 and 21 September, and the second dekad alone contributed 74.5mm, compared with 10.6mm in the first dekad and 37.1mm in the third. This was considerably wetter than the near-average rainfall forecast for Kilifi and the other coastal counties in the Kenya Meteorological Department's September outlook. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole has developed alongside a strengthening El Niño, a combination that normally enhances rainfall in eastern Kenya, and ICPAC's outlook points to a wetter October to December season.

daily_narrative: Kaguguta Agrifarm weather station recorded 9.80 mm of rain on 10 Oct, the second-largest daily amount of the dekad that closed that day. Oct-D1 2026 ended with a total of 33.9 mm, and rain fell on six days, four of them with more than 1 mm. The total came mainly from a few events. The 5–7 Oct window produced 22.4 mm, and 7 Oct alone contributed 16.8 mm, roughly half of the dekad's rain. The reading on 10 Oct added a further 9.80 mm, so these two events together account for about three-quarters of the total. Between them, 2–4 Oct and 9 Oct were dry, so the rain came in short episodes and was not spread evenly. The dekad total is roughly half of what October typically brings in a full month, which is a solid start to the season. It also fits the regional picture: the Kenya Meteorological Service declared the October–December short rains underway on 5 Oct, with rain reported in parts of the Coast. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole warms the western Indian Ocean and increases rainfall on the East African coast, and together with a strengthening El Niño it is the usual driver of enhanced short rains. The Australian Bureau of Meteorology still classes the dipole as neutral, with weekly index values of about +0.6 to +0.76 °C, and WMO expects the positive phase to peak in October. The ECMWF forecast points to a wetter dekad ahead, with a total of about 70 mm, which is roughly as much as October typically delivers in a full month.
